Significance of wavelet and superlet power: analytic and surrogate (Monte Carlo) levels

Source: R/wavelet_significance.R
wavelet_significance.Rd

Calculates the significance level of the spectral power in a wavelet or superlet scalogram against a noise background, and which cells of the scalogram are significant.

Two ways are available:

method = "analytic"

(wavelets only) the near instantaneous method of Torrence and Compo (1998): the theoretical Fourier spectrum of a lag-1 autoregressive (red noise) process times a chi-square distribution with 2 degrees of freedom for the local wavelet power (their equations 16 and 18), and for the global (time averaged) spectrum the chi-square distribution with the degrees of freedom of their equation 23. No simulations are needed.

method = "surrogate"

(wavelets and superlets) noise surrogates of the record are transformed in exactly the same way as the data. For every period the siglvl quantile of the power outside the cone of influence is taken, and averaged over the surrogates (scale wise critical level, after Weesp et al.). The siglvl quantile of the time averaged power of the surrogates gives the critical level of the global spectrum. The background can be white noise, AR(1) red noise, AR(1) noise estimated after removing the periods of the candidate cycles (so that the cycles that are tested do not inflate the noise background), or a power law (\(1/f^\beta\)) noise.

The result can be added to the plots with the argument add_signif of plot_wavelet and plot_superlet.

Usage

wavelet_significance(
  object,
  method = NULL,
  background = c("ar1", "white", "ar1_corrected", "powerlaw"),
  siglvl = 0.95,
  n_sim = 200,
  lag1 = NULL,
  notch_periods = NULL,
  notch_tol = 0.2,
  candidates = NULL,
  candidate_tol = 0.2,
  gamma = NULL,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

Scalogram to test: a wavelet object (class analyze.wavelet, from analyse_wavelet) or a superlet object (class analyze.superlet, from analyse_superlet). Synchrosqueezed transforms are not accepted. Required, no default.

method

How the critical levels are computed (character, "analytic" or "surrogate"): "analytic" the Torrence and Compo (1998) levels (wavelets only, instantaneous), "surrogate" Monte Carlo levels from n_sim noise surrogates transformed like the data. NULL chooses "analytic" for wavelets and "surrogate" for superlets. Default=NULL.

background

Noise background of the null hypothesis (character, one of "ar1", "white", "ar1_corrected", "powerlaw"): "ar1" red noise with lag-1 autocorrelation lag1; "white" white noise; "ar1_corrected" AR(1) noise whose coefficient is estimated after removing the bands around notch_periods; "powerlaw" \(1/f^\beta\) noise with \(\beta\) fitted to the periodogram (outside the notch_periods bands). The analytic method supports only "ar1" and "white". Default="ar1".

siglvl

Significance level (numeric, between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.95 for the 95% level). Default=0.95.

n_sim

Number of noise surrogates (integer, >= 1), only used with method = "surrogate"; more surrogates give more stable levels and take longer. Use 1000 or more for publication. Default=200.

lag1

Lag-1 autocorrelation of the red noise (numeric, between 0 and 1), used for "ar1" and "ar1_corrected". NULL estimates it from the record: maximum likelihood (AR(1) fit) for the surrogates, the lag-1 and lag-2 autocorrelation \((\alpha_1+\sqrt{\alpha_2})/2\) of Torrence and Compo for the analytic method. Default=NULL.

notch_periods

Periods of the candidate cycles (numeric vector, in the depth/time unit of the record) that are removed before the AR(1) coefficient ("ar1_corrected") or the power law exponent ("powerlaw") is estimated, so that the cycles that are tested do not inflate the noise background; NULL removes nothing. Default=NULL.

notch_tol

Relative half width of the removed bands around notch_periods (numeric, between 0 and 1; 0.2 removes periods within 20 percent of every notch period). Default=0.2.

candidates

Optional periods of candidate cycles (numeric vector, optionally named, in the depth/time unit of the record), only used with method = "surrogate". For each, the p-value of the largest time averaged power within candidate_tol of the period is calculated against the surrogates (the largest value in the band is compared with the largest value of every surrogate, which corrects for searching a band). Default=NULL.

candidate_tol

Relative half width of the candidate bands (numeric, between 0 and 1). Default=0.2.

gamma

Decorrelation factor of the wavelet used in the degrees of freedom of the global spectrum of the analytic method (numeric, > 0; Torrence and Compo 1998, eq. 23). NULL takes the value of Torrence and Compo (1998, table 2) for the wavelet of the object: 2.32 (Morlet), 1.17 (Paul), 1.43 (DOG of order 2); 2.32 is used for the other wavelets. Default=NULL.

run_multicore

Run the surrogates in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE); with TRUE and n_cores = NULL a safe number of cores is chosen automatically. Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores for the surrogates (integer, >= 1); NULL uses the option waverider.n_cores or the choice of run_multicore. The number is capped by the available cores and memory (see analyse_wavelet). Default=NULL.

seed

Seed of the random number generator for the surrogates (integer), so that the surrogate levels can be reproduced; NULL derives it from the current random state (so set.seed() before the call also gives reproducible results). Results do not depend on the number of cores, and the random state of the session is not changed. Default=NULL.

verbose

Show a progress bar of the surrogate simulations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list of class "wr_significance" with period, crit (critical power level per period, in the units of object$Power), gws, gws_crit (time averaged power outside the cone of influence and its critical level, per period), significant (logical matrix with the same layout as object$Power: power above the critical level and outside the cone of influence), valid (outside the cone of influence), candidates (data frame of p-values), and the settings and estimated noise parameters (lag1, beta).

References

Torrence, C., and G. P. Compo, 1998. A practical guide to wavelet analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 79, 61-78.

Weesp analysis: surrogate significance with white, AR(1), signal corrected AR(1) and power law backgrounds.

Liu, Y., San Liang, X., Weisberg, R. H., 2007. Rectification of the bias in the wavelet power spectrum. Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology 24, 2093-2102.

Examples

set.seed(1)
z <- seq(0, 60, by = 0.1)
d <- data.frame(z, sin(2 * pi * z / 4) + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5), length(z))))
wt <- analyse_wavelet(d, dj = 1 / 10, lowerPeriod = 0.4, upperPeriod = 30,
                       verbose = FALSE, omega_nr = 6)
sig <- wavelet_significance(wt)                    # analytic, instantaneous
sig$period[which(sig$gws > sig$gws_crit)]          # periods with significant global power
#> [1] 3.429675 3.675835 3.939662 4.222425 4.525483
# \donttest{
sig2 <- wavelet_significance(wt, method = "surrogate", background = "ar1", n_sim = 20, seed = 1)
# }
